steps.content: On (month redacted) 4, the intelligence agency located the last known batch of Mania Crystals in Syndicate. On the same day, the MBCC set up a special task force targeting this specific batch of the dangerous substance.

On (month redacted) 6, led personally by the MBCC's Chief, the special task force raided an underground hideout and captured the Thou Voodoos members there. Despite that, the task force was unable to find the targeted Mania Crystals in the hideout.

During (month redacted) 7 to 16, the task force continued to search for the remnants of Thou Voodoos in Syndicate. The MBCC captured and interrogated two hundred people within a week but obtained no insightful leads due to the complexity of the gang.
On (month redacted) 16, a small-scale Mania outbreak was seen in a certain neighborhood. The MBCC found a small amount of Mania Crystals on one of the deceased.

On (month redacted) 18, the MBCC captured three Thou Voodoos members on the loose during a raid. They later claimed in their interrogation that the Mania Crystals possessed by Thou Voodoos had already been stolen ten days ago.
And the culprit is another organization that's been lurking in Syndicate for a long time, the Homeless.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Crache is ready, Chief. You may begin anytime.
Got it.
You close the file on the desk and draw in a deep breath, fighting the fatigue.
Still, when you stand up, the pain in your prefrontal lobe makes you stumble slightly.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Perhaps you should get some rest first? You haven't slept in almost two days.
The lead didn't come easy. I can't slack off at this juncture.
Also, I don't think I can get a good night's sleep before this crisis of Mania Crystals is resolved.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I see...
Nightingale seems to think of something and reminds you again.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Please don't let your guard down with Crache.
You get what Nightingale means: don't have any unrealistic expectations or mercy. Before she's a child, Crache is first an extremely dangerous S-Class Sinner.
Don't worry. I've got this.
Seeing you walk into the interrogation room, Crache simply lifts her gaze once, then looks away.
Under the halogen lamp, her skin has a sickly pallor to it, a sharp contrast to the deep shadows under her eyes.
The truth is, even without Nightingale's warning and the knowledge of her S-Class Sinner identity, you can tell she's no ordinary kid.
You don't look too well. Have you not had any proper rest since coming here?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Heh...
She snickers in response.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Look at yourself.
You know you're in a bad shape now, but she's not saying this because she cares. She's only giving you an obvious warning.
Of course, to these Sinners born in Syndicate, starting a conversation with kindness is no different than baring your weakness.
The tough living conditions make them naturally vigilant to kindness. It's probably wiser to start with a stern attitude.
To these Sinners born in Syndicate, starting a conversation with kindness is no different than baring your weakness.
A stern attitude may make communication more effective, but be sure not to provoke them too much. After all, even the shackles can't guarantee absolute safety in the face of S-Class Sinners.
You take a deep breath to keep your mind clear. Then, you cut to the chase.
Let's talk about the Homeless.
Crache didn't answer, but you see an expression in between vigilance and threat on her face.
She doesn't like to hear those words from you, the Homeless.

You hand the report to Crache.
The Homeless has quite a wide range of services. From what I see in this report, I may even think it's a gang which has existed before BR-004.
The several Sinners in the Homeless have accomplished many things even adults cannot...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: What are you getting at?
Crache doesn't even glimpse at the report once and interrupts you with a frown.
Nothing. I just think you're different from ordinary kids. You guys are outstanding.
You are outstanding.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: What does that have to do with me?
Aren't you the boss of the Homeless?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Where did you learn that?
I asked the members of the Homeless, of course...
Having said that, you feel the air tenses up instantly. Crache's face turns scarily gloomy.
Relax, I asked them in a different setting, not like this. After all, the Homeless had never been involved with Mania before this. They're not the MBCC's responsibility.
They didn't tell me your name. They only told me to piss off and stay away from their territory.
That if I dared mess with the Homeless, their Guardian would surely find me and erase me permanently.
Crache stares at you slightly suspiciously, the mysteriously dangerous air about her slowly fading. After a moment of silence, she says coolly.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: They were lying to you.
They might have reasons to lie, but those gangsters didn't.
My people grilled more than twenty former gangsters under the Executive Committee's control. They came from Yagyu, Red Falcon, and Thou Voodoos.
Wanna hear what they had to say about the Homeless?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Like I care.
After a pause, she says again emphatically.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: I don't want to know.

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: "Dregs, little brats, scoundrels, vermin..."

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: "But no matter what crappy deeds they've done, as long as they're some kids who know how to paint that ugly graffiti, that ******* Sinner will watch over them."

steps.speaker: Gangster
steps.content: "She comes and goes in the shadows. No one can get her. Plus, she's like a ******* mad dog, you can't reason with her. Every Syndican gang has been tricked by her badly before."
Hearing you relay the gangsters' complaints, Crache reacts a little differently than you expected.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Hahaha, how funny. These adults who have no skills other than committing crimes think the kids are being unreasonable... Who are they to judge?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: The rulers of Syndicate who rode roughshod over everyone throughout the years? Now that someone finally overpowers them, they're acting like crybabies with you?
I know what those gangsters have done in Syndicate, but that has nothing to do with their testimonies. The Guardian of the Homeless and that Sinner they described, it's you, isn't it?
Or perhaps, you can tell me if there's another Sinner in Syndicate whose power is comparable to that of yours and has a motive to help the Homeless frequently?
Crache looks at you with amusement and answers.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: So you believe them? Believe a bunch of heartless Syndican gangsters would get frightened to death by a random kid?
Crache's response makes you momentarily speechless.
At least regarding this, they didn't have a reason to lie, and they couldn't have colluded with one another.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Haha, is that so?
Crache has lost the interest to argue with you further.
You can keep on denying it. But regardless, you've got some kind of connection with the Homeless, haven't you?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Tsk...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: What do you want? Do you want me to threaten the Homeless for you? You're barking up the wrong tree.
No, I'm not going to threaten the Homeless.
You collect the report from the desk and look straight at Crache, flashing her a smile.
It doesn't matter whether you're their guardian or leader or not. Sure, if you are, it'll make things a lot easier.
I have a matter of utmost importance to verify with the leader of the Homeless.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: I have no interest in being a messenger.
It concerns the Homeless and even the safety of the entire Syndicate. I hope you could cooperate with me.
Crache remains silent after that. She knows you're a tricky opponent, but she seems unmotivated by your serious request and doesn't so much as glance at you.
It doesn't unsettle you. You have enough information on hand to make her waver.

Fourteen days ago, the MBCC discovered that the remnants of Thou Voodoos held a batch of Mania Crystals. But after going through most of these remaining Thou Voodoos members, we still weren't able to find the Mania Crystals.
At the mention of Mania Crystals, Crache frowns conspicuously. Clearly, she knows about that thing.
Considering the relations between Crache and the Homeless, you know your next sentence will turn this interrogation over completely.
We're convinced that the Homeless has stolen this batch of Mania Crystals from Thou Voodoos.
Crache jerks her head up, a look of disbelief on her face.
But the expression vanished quickly and she regained her cool. She bows her head slightly and says in an almost eerie tone.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: For your own good, joke about something else.
The excessive grimness on the surface means she's wavering inside. This piece of news has completely gone beyond her expectation.

"Beginning (month redacted), the Homeless has become abnormally active. Both the frequency and severity of their acts have gone up. They've even begun planned and organized illegal activities."
"On (month redacted) 18, the Bureau arrested three Thou Voodoos members. They claimed that the Mania Crystals had been stolen by the Homeless. Their testimonies are as follows..."

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Cut it out.
Crache glares intently at the document on the desk. Her voice is glum and harsh.
I assume you know nothing about this, do you?
Crache doesn't respond directly. Her expression is so dark that she no longer looks like a child.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...Have you done anything to the Homeless?
No. Their members are very alert. We've had great difficulty getting in touch with them.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: You don't know much about the Homeless?
Indeed. That's why I hope you could provide the relevant information. I need to verify with them whether this series of incidents is true.
Can you tell me where they're located? Or a way I can communicate with them?

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Haha.
Crache snickers, as if mocking your naivety.
Let me try again. Is it possible that while you were away, some other power instructed or threatened the Homeless to...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: No.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: They wouldn't dare.
Crache's tone is calm and matter-of-fact.
That leaves us with another possibility...
The Homeless did plan this and stole the Mania Crystals from Thou Voodoos.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...This is all just your speculation. The Homeless is nothing more than a bunch of kids. They're not capable of that.
Contrary to the previous firm denial, Crache shows a brief hesitation this time.

But based on the information we have, the Homeless has skills comparable to those of a professional thief gang. It's not entirely impossible that they could have stolen the Mania Crystals from the gangsters.
They could have acted on their own while you were away...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: We're not idiots.
...You seem to be fully aware of the danger of Mania Crystals. But can you guarantee every one of the over one thousand members of the Homeless does too?
Suppose they all do, but what if they didn't know those were Mania Crystals before they acted?

steps.speaker: Narration
steps.content: Crache's face is growing more and more ashen.
I wish I didn't have to suspect the Homeless either, Crache, but they're not beyond suspicion.
As soon as the Homeless got in direct contact with the Mania Crystals, this has become bigger than them... We can't just sit back and do nothing.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Can't just sit back and do nothing... Hahaha...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Then why didn't you do anything when those parentless little punks were dying in Syndicate?
It's neither a hysterical scream nor an emotional accusation. Her attitude is cold and sarcastic, as if she's only a bratty kid making some mean joke.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Just when we've found a way to survive, you servants of justice finally decide to show up.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Telling us to always think of the greater good, to consider the safety of Syndicate...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: What does your greater good matter to the Homeless?
The look on Crache's face is so indifferent that it's almost cold.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Though I have to admit... First the Public Security Bureau, then the Executive Committee, then you...

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: From colluding with the gangsters to pretending we don't exist, to these gentle talks... At least you've learned how to act like it.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: But you're no different than them. You just want to use us.
No, that's never been my intention. I only want to help.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Oh?
There's an icy sarcasm in Crache's voice.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: If it's not because of the Mania Crystals, will you still give a damn about the Homeless?
Before you answer, Crache lifts her head and looks into your eyes again.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: You won't, none of you will. We can only count on ourselves.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: The greatest help you adults can give us is to stay away from the Homeless and stop bothering us.
Alright, I see what you mean, and I trust that you have a genuine bond with the Homeless.
But can you really be certain that the Homeless has nothing to do with this Mania Crystal incident?
A muscle twitches on Crache's face. She presses her lips tightly together. Even so, she can't hide the look in her eyes.
Her distrust of adults and bias toward the Homeless have been outweighed by her concern for her companions' safety.
Consider this, what if someone from the Homeless really did steal the Mania Crystals? Can they really handle this situation safely on their own?
Your words have finally shaken Crache's attitude. She can no longer conceal the anxiety on her face.
Crache, we're not against each other on this. We can cooperate.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: I don't need to cooperate with anyone. I can handle it on my own.
...I know you can't trust me easily, and you think I want to take advantage of you. But this is really not something that you or the Homeless can resolve on your own.
Without the proper equipment, you can't even dispose of the Mania Crystals safely without harming yourselves.
You press on the pulsing vein on the side of your head and go on explaining patiently.
The Homeless... are only a group of children, after all. Whether or not they've touched the Mania Crystals, they'll always be the most vulnerable bunch.
I don't want them to face this kind of danger. We agree on this at least, don't we?
I need your help. More precisely, the Homeless needs your help.
Brow tightly wrinkled, Crache ponders what you've said and stays silent for a long moment.
After an almost too-long, repressing silence, she finally speaks.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...One person.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Just you, and me. No one else follows us.
At this, you finally press on your chest and exhale deeply. Your tireless persuasion and unreserved honesty finally pay off. You even feel the days of accumulated exhaustion suddenly all vanish.
Seeing your reaction, Crache says with a snicker.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Don't get carried away.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: If I notice you're lying to me or doing anything that can harm the Homeless... The shadow will follow you.
Smiling, you wave your hand.
That won't happen.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Haha, try not to have too much faith in your shackles... Chief.
